views.name: qualifying_q1_times_ms
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.qualifyId,
  q.raceId,
  q.driverId,
  q.q1,
  CASE
    WHEN q.q1 IS NULL THEN NULL
    -- format like M:SS.mmm or SS.mmm or M:SS.mm
    WHEN instr(q.q1, ':') > 0 THEN
      (
        CAST(substr(q.q1, 1, instr(q.q1, ':') - 1) AS INTEGER) * 60000
        + CAST(substr(q.q1, instr(q.q1, ':') + 1, instr(q.q1 || '.', '.') - instr(q.q1, ':') - 1) AS INTEGER) * 1000
        + CAST(
            printf('%-3s', substr(q.q1, instr(q.q1, '.') + 1))
            AS INTEGER
          )
      )
    WHEN instr(q.q1, '.') > 0 THEN
      (
        CAST(substr(q.q1, 1, instr(q.q1, '.') - 1) AS INTEGER) * 1000
        + CAST(
            printf('%-3s', substr(q.q1, instr(q.q1, '.') + 1))
            AS INTEGER
          )
      )
    ELSE
      NULL
  END AS q1_milliseconds
FROM qualifying_rows q
WHERE q.q1 IS NOT NULL
views.description: Normalized view converting qualifying.q1 textual lap times into milliseconds where possible, preserving original q1 text. One row per qualifying record. Useful to rank/sort drivers by Q1 performance.

views.name: qualifying_q2_times_millis
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.qualifyId,
  q.raceId,
  q.driverId,
  q.q2,
  CASE
    WHEN q.q2 GLOB '*:*.*' THEN
      (
        -- formats like M:SS.mmm or MM:SS.mmm
        (CAST(substr(q.q2, 1, instr(q.q2, ':')-1) AS INTEGER) * 60 * 1000)
        + (CAST(substr(q.q2, instr(q.q2, ':')+1, instr(q.q2, '.') - instr(q.q2, ':') - 1) AS INTEGER) * 1000)
        + CAST(substr(q.q2, instr(q.q2, '.')+1) AS INTEGER)
      )
    WHEN q.q2 GLOB '*:*' AND q.q2 NOT GLOB '*.*' THEN
      (
        -- formats like M:SS (no milliseconds)
        (CAST(substr(q.q2, 1, instr(q.q2, ':')-1) AS INTEGER) * 60 * 1000)
        + (CAST(substr(q.q2, instr(q.q2, ':')+1) AS INTEGER) * 1000)
      )
    WHEN q.q2 GLOB '*.*' AND instr(q.q2, ':') = 0 THEN
      (
        -- formats like SS.mmm (seconds.milliseconds)
        (CAST(substr(q.q2, 1, instr(q.q2, '.')-1) AS INTEGER) * 1000)
        + CAST(substr(q.q2, instr(q.q2, '.')+1) AS INTEGER)
      )
    ELSE
      NULL
  END AS q2_milliseconds
FROM qualifying_rows q
WHERE q.q2 IS NOT NULL
views.description: Normalized qualifying q2 times converted to milliseconds where possible, preserving original q2 text and linking to driver and race. One row per qualifying record (qualifyId).

views.name: qualifying_q3_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.qualifyId,
  q.raceId,
  q.driverId,
  q.number,
  q.q3,
  CASE
    WHEN q.q3 IS NULL THEN NULL
    -- q3 formats expected like M:SS.mmm or S:MM.mmm or SS.mmm; convert to milliseconds
    WHEN INSTR(q.q3, ':') = 0 THEN
      -- no minutes separator, assume seconds.milliseconds
      (CAST(SUBSTR(q.q3, 1, INSTR(q.q3, '.') - 1) AS INTEGER) * 1000)
      + CAST(SUBSTR(q.q3, INSTR(q.q3, '.') + 1) AS INTEGER)
    ELSE
      -- has minutes part
      (CAST(SUBSTR(q.q3, 1, INSTR(q.q3, ':') - 1) AS INTEGER) * 60 * 1000)
      + (CAST(SUBSTR(q.q3, INSTR(q.q3, ':') + 1, INSTR(q.q3, '.') - INSTR(q.q3, ':') - 1) AS INTEGER) * 1000)
      + CAST(SUBSTR(q.q3, INSTR(q.q3, '.') + 1) AS INTEGER)
  END AS q3_milliseconds
FROM qualifying_rows q
views.description: A view exposing qualifying records with canonicalized q3 and q3 milliseconds (if available) to make exact and normalized time filters easier.

    WHEN (fastestLapSpeed GLOB '*[0-9]*') THEN CAST(replace(replace(fastestLapSpeed, ',', ''), ' ', '') AS REAL)

views.name: race_results_fastestlap_speed_clean
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  resultId,
  raceId,
  driverId,
  constructorId,
  fastestLapSpeed AS fastestLapSpeed_raw,
  CASE
    WHEN fastestLapSpeed IS NULL THEN NULL
    -- remove any non-digit/decimal characters like 'km/h', spaces, plus signs, etc.
    -- SQLite lacks regexp_replace; use nested REPLACE to strip common suffixes and commas
    ELSE
      NULLIF(
        -- try to coerce cleaned string to numeric; if empty then NULL
        (CASE
           WHEN trim(
             replace(
               replace(
                 replace(
                   replace(fastestLapSpeed, 'km/h', ''),
                 'kph', ''),
               '+', ''),
             ' ', '')
           ) = '' THEN NULL
           ELSE
             -- final attempt: cast cleaned string to real
             CAST(
               trim(
                 replace(
                   replace(
                     replace(
                       replace(fastestLapSpeed, 'km/h', ''),
                     'kph', ''),
                   '+', ''),
                 ' ', '')
               ) AS REAL
             )
         END)
      , 0) -- keep 0 as valid numeric; NULLIF used to avoid returning 0 for empty -> will return NULL
  END AS fastestLapSpeed
FROM results
WHERE fastestLapSpeed IS NOT NULL
views.description: One row per result (per raceId and driverId) projecting fastestLapSpeed as a numeric measure parsed from results.fastestLapSpeed and exposing key identifiers for filtering and joining.

WHERE d.dob IS NOT NULL
views.description: Prepares driver-level age measures computed from dob to support age-based comparisons (one row per driver with computed age in years as a numeric measure). Keeps raw dob and computed age for filtering/sorting.

views.name: races_with_circuit_48
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  races.raceId AS raceId,
  races.name AS "races.name",
  races.date AS "races.date",
  circuits.circuitId AS circuitId,
  circuits.name AS "circuits.name",
  circuits.location AS "circuits.location",
  circuits.country AS "circuits.country",
  circuits.lat AS "circuits.lat",
  circuits.lng AS "circuits.lng"
FROM races
LEFT JOIN circuits ON races.circuitId = circuits.circuitId
views.description: One row per race with its associated circuit attributes (denormalized races + circuits). Useful for queries that need race details together with circuit name, location, country, and coordinates.

views.name: circuits_canonical
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  circuitId,
  circuitRef,
  name,
  location,
  country,
  lat,
  lng
FROM circuits
views.description: Canonicalized circuit attributes exposing circuit id, canonical name, location, country and lat/lng for geographical or location-based queries. Normalizes column names to stable outputs used by other views.

views.name: results_with_race
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.resultId AS resultId,
  r.raceId AS raceId,
  r.driverId AS driverId,
  r.constructorId AS constructorId,
  r.points AS points,
  r.milliseconds AS milliseconds,
  r.position AS position,
  r.positionText AS positionText,
  races.name AS race_name,
  races.year AS race_year
FROM results r
JOIN races ON r.raceId = races.raceId
views.description: Race results denormalized with race metadata (name, year) to support queries about performance by race and driver. Keeps raw timing and points fields; excludes rows with NULL milliseconds if desired at query time.

views.name: driver_fastest_lap_per_driver
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  results.driverId AS driverId,
  MIN(results.milliseconds) AS min_milliseconds
FROM results
WHERE results.milliseconds IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY results.driverId
views.description: For each driver, the single minimum non-null result milliseconds observed across all their results (one row per driver). Exposes the driverId and the min milliseconds to enable finding which race(s) achieved that min when joined back to results.

views.name: drivers_core_52
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  driverId,
  forename,
  surname,
  (forename || CASE WHEN forename IS NOT NULL AND surname IS NOT NULL THEN ' ' ELSE '' END || COALESCE(surname, '')) AS full_name,
  dob,
  nationality,
  driverRef
FROM drivers
views.description: Canonical driver rows with stable id and full name; useful for any driver-level filtering or join. Keeps raw identity and name parts without applying question-specific filters.

views.name: results_by_race_driver
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.resultId,
  r.raceId,
  r.driverId,
  r.constructorId,
  r.points,
  r.position,
  r.positionText,
  r.positionOrder,
  r.laps,
  r.time,
  r.milliseconds,
  r.fastestLap,
  r.fastestLapTime,
  r.fastestLapSpeed,
  r.statusId
FROM results AS r
views.description: One row per race-result (a driver entry in a race) combining results with driver and race keys and raw measures (points, position). Suitable for finding earliest participation, points per race, and other per-entry analyses.

views.name: races_core_54
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  races.raceId AS raceId,
  races.year AS year,
  races.round AS round,
  races.name AS name,
  races.date AS date,
  races.circuitId AS circuitId,
  circuits.location AS location,
  circuits.country AS country
FROM races
LEFT JOIN circuits ON races.circuitId = circuits.circuitId
views.description: One row per race with primary identifying and geographic/date/name fields; useful as the base cohort for questions about races, locations, and names.

views.name: race_name_counts_by_country
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.name AS race_name,
  c.country AS country,
  COUNT(*) AS race_count
FROM races r
JOIN circuits c ON r.circuitId = c.circuitId
GROUP BY r.name, c.country
views.description: Aggregate counts of races by race name and circuit country. Keeps counts at the (race name, country) level so callers can compute proportions or totals and filter to any specific race name or country.
